marketRegime.rationale: Crude reversed from the mid-August squeeze and long yields eased off multi-decade highs, but Eurozone inflation near 3% and a Jackson Hole address on Friday keep the risk elevated rather than benign.

executivePulse.title: Crude reverses
executivePulse.text: Brent at $88.88 after a third straight decline, with crude closing over 3% lower as Washington shifted to economic rather than military pressure on Iran. The August squeeze thesis toward $94 has unwound.

executivePulse.title: Yields ease
executivePulse.text: The US 10-year eased to 4.64% from about 4.70%, lowering borrowing costs globally, though the 30-year touched 5.327% earlier this month — its highest since June 2007.

executivePulse.title: Europe's inflation floor
executivePulse.text: Eurozone CPI was 2.9% in July and the ECB's Lane expects it near 3% through 2026, with the Bund at 3.26%, the highest since 2008. European financing conditions stay tight.

catalysts.title: US PCE inflation print (Fed's preferred gauge)
Nvidia earnings — bellwether for the AI trade
Jackson Hole: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks

globalBriefing: Crude's reversal is the week's pivot: Brent at $88.88 after a third consecutive decline, as the United States moved to economic rather than military pressure on Iran, unwinding the sanctions-squeeze thesis that drove the 22 August briefing. Long yields eased in parallel — the US 10-year to 4.64% — lifting the S&P 500 to 7,677 and the Stoxx 600 by 0.35%, while gold's 1.78% advance to $4,461 shows the hedge has not been unwound with it. Europe is the laggard: inflation at 2.9% with the ECB guiding to near 3% through 2026, and a Bund at 2008 highs, keep regional financing conditions tight even as global risk eases.
marketOpen: Wednesday's US PCE print and Nvidia earnings land on the same day, with Chair Warsh at Jackson Hole on Friday — three catalysts capable of reversing the easing in yields that is currently supporting equities.

macro.description: Central bank decisions, inflation prints, GDP, yield curves, and FX
macro.keyTakeaway: If the PCE print confirms the easing in long yields, European credit stays the laggard rather than the leader, because the ECB is guiding to inflation near 3% through year-end.

items.headline: US 10-year Treasury yield eases to 4.64% ahead of July PCE print
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Treasuries retreated across the curve ahead of the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, with the 10-year easing from about 4.70% the previous session and lowering borrowing costs globally.
items.relevance: Lower long yields relieve refinancing pressure on leveraged real assets, but the move is positioning ahead of a print rather than a confirmed trend.

items.headline: Eurozone inflation at 2.9% in July; ECB's Lane guides to near 3% for the rest of 2026
items.summary: According to reporting on ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane's remarks, inflation is expected to hold near 3% through the remainder of 2026, with the German Bund at 3.26%, its highest level since 2008.
items.relevance: A 3% inflation floor caps the scope for ECB easing and keeps European financing costs elevated relative to the US.

items.headline: Brazil's central bank cuts Selic 25 basis points to 14.00% in fourth consecutive reduction
items.summary: Per Rio Times, the cut extends an easing sequence, with the Ibovespa closing at 174,576.80 (+1.55%) and the real at 5.14 per dollar.
items.relevance: A sustained LatAm easing cycle supports local-currency debt and equity risk in the region while developed-market policy stays restrictive.

items.headline: US strategy on Iran shifts from military escalation to economic pressure
items.summary: Per CNBC, the change in approach eased market fears of renewed war in the Persian Gulf and was the proximate driver of the third consecutive decline in crude.
items.relevance: Removes the tail risk that drove August's freight and energy repricing, without resolving the underlying dispute.

items.headline: Crude closes more than 3% lower as US shifts to economic pressure on Iran
items.summary: Per CNBC, prices fell for a third consecutive session as the United States moved to a strategy of economic pressure on Iran, easing fears of renewed conflict in the Persian Gulf. Brent settled at $88.88 and WTI at $83.11.
items.relevance: The reversal removes the supply-disruption premium that underpinned the constructive energy stance taken on 22 August.

items.headline: Gold advances 1.78% to $4,461/oz despite the equity rally
items.summary: Per Rio Times, gold rose even as the three major US indices closed higher and the dollar index held near 99.
items.relevance: Safe-haven demand persisting through an equity rally suggests the risk-on move is positioning, not conviction.
